The draft answers Marisol's question head-on: "Short answer: no." It explains why. She went over the plan every day, ran an unplanned Monday, and her effort was almost double her three-week average. It also sets a clear rule to follow the plan line. That matters here because she jumped from 37 to 53 miles against a 38-mile plan.

Next week adds up to 44 miles (6+9+6+5+18). That's a sensible middle point: a real step down from the 53 she ran, and a moderate step up from the planned 38. The long run drops from 20 to 18 miles. There's no sharp jump in either, and Monday and Friday stay as rest days. Every day can be run as written, with paces and heart-rate caps.

Weaknesses:
- The visible text never mentions her tight calves, not even a "tell me if it lingers" check, even though the plan has pace work on Wednesday and Sunday.
- Saying it is "holding volume steady" is a little off, since the plan actually cuts from 53.
- The card doesn't mention the 20-mile run or the company, so those details can't be checked.

The tightness is mild and she says she otherwise feels great, so this isn't an injury sign that needed a referral. Overall the plan is safe and well fitted to her.
